core: The major hotel divisions and departments: rooms division (front office + reservations + housekeeping), food and beverage, sales and marketing, human resources, engineering/maintenance, security, accounting/finance
Revenue centers versus support (cost) centers and how departments are classified
How departments interrelate through the general manager, the executive committee, and the daily operating cycle
The rooms division as the typical largest revenue producer
supporting: USALI as the lodging industry's standard departmental chart of accounts
Lodging manager occupational role, wage, and outlook (BLS)
Naming-level mention of occupancy, ADR, and RevPAR as performance metrics

claims.claim: Hotels organize into specialized departments that are sorted into revenue centers (which sell directly to guests) and support/cost centers (which enable those sales without billing guests).
The rooms division combines the front office, reservations, and housekeeping, and in most hotels generates more revenue than any other division.

Food and beverage is typically the second revenue center, operating restaurants, bars, room service, and banquet/catering, and is generally less profitable per dollar of sales than rooms because it is more labor- and inventory-intensive.
Support centers such as engineering/maintenance, human resources, accounting/finance, security, and sales and marketing sustain operations but do not take money directly from guests.
A general manager, supported by an executive committee of division and department heads, coordinates the departments, sets budgets, and resolves cross-department trade-offs.

The Uniform System of Accounts for the Lodging Industry (USALI), first issued in 1926 and now in its 12th edition (published 2024), is the standard chart of accounts that reports each hotel department as its own profit center so properties can be compared.

Lodging managers coordinate front-office, housekeeping, maintenance, and food service; the occupation had a median annual wage of $68,130 in May 2024 across about 52,000 jobs, with employment projected to grow roughly 3 percent from 2024 to 2034.
Hotel performance is tracked with a small shared set of metrics, principally occupancy, average daily rate (ADR), and revenue per available room (RevPAR).

The front office runs a nightly night audit that reconciles the day's guest charges and closes the accounting day; a property management system ties reservations, front desk, housekeeping, and billing together.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether reservations is a separate department or part of the front office, and whether security sits inside the rooms division.
positions: Some texts fold reservations and communications into the front office and list security as its own department
Others list reservations and uniformed/security services as distinct rooms-division components
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Presented at overview level as commonly grouped functions, noting that the exact department boundaries vary by property; the lesson does not assert one fixed org chart.
